title: Check If Word Is Valid After Substitutions
summary: Determine if the string s can be generated by starting with an empty string t and repeatedly inserting the substring "abc" into t at any position.
statement: Determine if the string s can be generated by starting with an empty string t and repeatedly inserting the substring "abc" into t at any position. Return true if s is valid according to this rule, otherwise return false.
constraints: Start from abc and repeatedly insert another abc anywhere.
Return whether s can be produced.
hints: Reverse the insertion process by removing every completed abc block.
A stack can remove a block as soon as its suffix becomes a,b,c.
Push each character; when the last three equal abc, delete them; accept an empty stack.
Immediate removal is safe because inserted blocks are properly nested or adjacent in the reverse construction.
editorial: Immediate removal is safe because inserted blocks are properly nested or adjacent in the reverse construction.

tests.explanation: Remove an inner abc and then the remaining abc, so the string is valid.
Removing the first abc leaves cba, so it is invalid.
